transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing some light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

So light gardening like gentle weeding should be fine after that first week, but try to avoid anything too demanding.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, regarding how to store it, you should check the bottle to see whether it needs to be kept in the fridge or at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for explaining that. I have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great! Is the light sensitivity mild, or is it quite severe? And is your eye red or painful at all?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: The light sensitivity is more on the mild side, and my eye isn't red or painful. But before I forget, I have one last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to hear that it's mild. For mild light sensitivity, I'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

Regarding your blurriness question - it's quite common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about two weeks ago. I have noticed some improvement, but there's still a bit of blurriness.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good that you've noticed some improvement. It's normal for vision to take a bit of time to settle down, and two weeks is still quite early. It should continue to improve over the coming weeks.

However, if your vision is getting significantly worse or remains quite blurry, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you, Dora, for the information and reassurance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you again for your help!
